title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working note inside the divided-power de Rham dossier. It is not connected to the neighbouring pages, which are typescript from SGA 7 IX on extensions panachées. Its topic is the duality between comodules over a commutative Hopf algebra (or coalgebra) S over a base ring k and modules over its dual 'hyperalgebra' S^h, meaning distributions or divided-power differential operators.

(1) Injectivity question. Assume C is flat over k and S embeds in a product k^I. The intended embedding is S → k^{S^h}, x ↦ (u(x))_{u∈S^h}, which is injective when the pairing is separating. Then C⊗_k S → C⊗_k k^I is injective by flatness. To compare a comodule C → C⊗S with Hom_k(S^h, C) = C^{S^h}, one also needs C⊗_k k^I → C^I to be injective. Grothendieck asks whether this holds. He first answers yes, 'by passage to the inductive limit on I, reduce to I finite'. He then hedges: 'conditions of flatness type on C, supposing it free over k'. Note that he writes k^{(I)}, the direct sum, for which the map is trivially injective, while the question concerns k^I, the product.

(2) Model example. Take S = k[U], the additive group G_a, with dual hyperalgebra S^h = k{{T}}, the divided-power algebra (an 'ordinary hyperalgebra'). Take C = k[U, Y_0, …, Y_n] with C^h = k{{T}}{{X_0, …, X_n}}, which is an S^h-algebra. The divided monomials T^{(i)} X_0^{(i_0)} … X_n^{(i_n)} act on C by the Hasse–Schmidt divided differential operators D_U^{(i)} D_{Y_0}^{(i_0)} … In particular S^h acts by the D_U^{(i)}.

(3) Remark. These actions are locally nilpotent: if deg P ≤ n and f has order > n, then D_f P = 0.

(4) General question. Let S^h be a cocommutative, unital hyperalgebra, free over k. Which S^h-module-algebra structures on C come from an S-comodule structure C → C⊗_k S ⊂ Hom_k(S^h, C)? The expected answer is the locally finite / locally nilpotent ('rational') ones. The last line compares C⊗_k Hom_k(S^h, k) with Hom_k(S^h, C⊗k), where (S^h)^∨ is the dual of S^h.

Purpose: to set up the dictionary 'G_a-type or formal-group actions ↔ locally nilpotent actions of divided-power differential operators'. This underlies a divided-power (crystalline-type) de Rham formalism.
errors: The argument 'by passage to the inductive limit on I one reduces to I finite' does not work for the product k^I. The product is not the inductive limit of the k^J for J finite (the direct sum k^{(I)} is). For k^{(I)} the map C⊗k^{(I)} → C^I is trivially injective.

For the product k^I, injectivity of C⊗_k k^I → C^I is not automatic for flat C. The correct general condition is of Mittag-Leffler type (Raynaud–Gruson). For C free (or projective) it does hold. Grothendieck's hedge 'supposing free over k' is the correct fix.
Several notations are loose: 'C⊗S → C⊗_S k^I' should be C⊗_k S → C⊗_k k^I, and S → k^{(S^h)} should be the product k^{S^h}.

ideas.what: Comodules over a coalgebra S correspond to locally finite ('rational') modules over the dual algebra S^h, provided C⊗S → Hom(S^h, C) is injective (flatness / Mittag-Leffler type conditions).
ideas.modern_name: Rational modules over the dual algebra; comodule–module correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier; Sweedler (Hopf Algebras, 1969); Demazure–Gabriel (1970); Raynaud–Gruson for the Mittag-Leffler part
ideas.where_published: Related material in SGA 3 (Exp. I, on representations and comodules)

ideas.what: The distribution algebra of G_a is the divided-power algebra k{{T}}, acting on polynomial rings by Hasse–Schmidt divided derivatives D^{(i)}.
ideas.modern_name: Hyperalgebra / distribution algebra Dist(G_a); Hasse–Schmidt derivations

ideas.what: These actions are locally nilpotent (an operator of order > deg P kills P), and the question is which hyperalgebra actions integrate to comodule (group) actions.
ideas.modern_name: Locally nilpotent iterative higher derivations ↔ G_a-actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; Miyanishi and others in affine algebraic geometry

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard comodule/hyperalgebra duality and Hasse–Schmidt operators, worked out as scratch for the divided-power de Rham project. It contains a small, self-corrected gap about products versus direct sums and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'S → k^{(S^h)}' is meant as the product k^{S^h}.
'C ⊗ S → C ⊗_S k^I' should read C ⊗_k S → C ⊗_k k^I.
The word read as 'diff.' in 'opère par l'op. diff.' is uncertain in the image.
